spec.goal: Add a restrained outside-only white dashed border for drag and Frozen selections so the boundary stays readable on very dark content without reintroducing the old glow-heavy frozen treatment.
success_criteria: Live drag selection renders a static white dashed border outside the focus rect while preserving the existing bright-inside plus dimmed-outside treatment.
Frozen selection renders the same outside-only dashed border whenever a non-fullscreen frozen capture rect is visible.
Fullscreen fallback renders no extra border, and edge-aligned selections clip naturally instead of pushing the border into captured pixels.
The new border stays visually lightweight and does not restore the previous animated frozen border language.
Focused overlay tests cover the fullscreen skip behavior and the outside-border geometry path.
constraints: Keep the implementation scoped to overlay affordance rendering; do not modify capture/export pixel data paths.
Do not reintroduce animated Frozen border effects.
Do not draw the dashed border inside the capture rect except where screen-edge clipping naturally removes outside space.
Use repo-native Rust verification before claiming completion.

outputs: Static dashed-border constants and helper(s) with fullscreen skip logic
verification: Renderer-local helpers compile cleanly and keep the border outside the focus rect when outside space exists.

tasks.objective: Render the shared outside-only dashed border on top of the existing scrim treatment for live drag and Frozen selection states without affecting hover-flow behavior.
outputs: Updated scrim render path that draws the agreed border only for non-fullscreen selection rects
verification: Live drag and Frozen selection both use the same dashed border treatment.
Fullscreen fallback still draws no border.
